facility_roles.quote: The Solenoidal Tracker at RHIC, known as STAR, tracks the thousands of particles produced by ion collisions at RHIC.

intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: End date is the day of RHIC's 25th and final run's final collisions; see the terminal interval below. The BNL page's own '2000-2026' range appears to be generated relative to the current year rather than a fixed historical statement, so the 2026 end bound is corroborated independently via the final-collisions article rather than relied on alone.

intervals.label: RHIC 25th and final run ends
intervals.locator: BNL Newsroom, "A Smashing Success: Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider Wraps up Final Collisions", 2026-02
intervals.note: Marks the end of RHIC operations in the 25th and final run. BNL states the RHIC science mission continues 'until we analyze all the data and publish all the papers.' BNL, 13 April 2026: STAR, "which captured the first collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) in 2000 and ran through every RHIC run until Feb. 6, 2026, will be taken apart to make way for the new ePIC detector being designed and constructed for the Electron-Ion Collider"; the STAR interaction region becomes the site of ePIC. Disassembly is part of a six-year removal programme begun 13 April 2026; no source fetched reports that STAR's disassembly has started, so the status stays completed (operations ended), not decommissioned.
intervals.quote: crashed into one another at nearly the speed of light inside the collider's two house-sized particle detectors, STAR and sPHENIX.

The overview paper is retained as an identity/detector-paper citation only (locator, no quote).

STAR magnet field strength (commonly reported elsewhere as approx. 0.5 T) is not recorded: no source consulted gave it verbatim (the STAR magnet subsystem paper, NIM A499:633-639, returned 403 or empty on every fetch attempt), so it is left out rather than sourced from a search-engine paraphrase.

physics_goals.quote: search for signatures of the form of matter that RHIC was designed to create: the quark-gluon plasma
physics_goals.value: Detect and characterize the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed in heavy-ion collisions

summary.plain: STAR was a house-sized, 1,200-tonne particle detector at Brookhaven National Laboratory that watched gold and other heavy atomic nuclei smash together from 2000 until RHIC's final run ended in February 2026, looking for a hot, liquid-like state of matter called the quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: Solenoidal Tracker at RHIC: a large-acceptance heavy-ion collider experiment centred on a 4 m diameter x 4.2 m long Time Projection Chamber providing full-azimuth charged-particle tracking within |η| < 1.8, studying quark-gluon plasma formation in Au+Au and other collision systems at RHIC from 2000 through RHIC's 25th and final run, which concluded 2026-02-06.

unique_capabilities.quote: The TPC provides complete coverage around the beam-line, and provides complete tracking for charged particles within +- 1.8 units of pseudo-rapidity of the center-of-mass frame.
unique_capabilities.value: A large-acceptance Time Projection Chamber providing complete azimuthal tracking of charged particles within about 1.8 units of pseudorapidity, reconstructing thousands of tracks per collision event
